newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban militia capture Bagram military airbase.
newsitem.headline: Taleban militia capture Bagram military airbase.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban militia captured the Bagram military airbase north of Kabul on Thursday, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press quoted witnesses as saying the Taleban had gained control of the base after a fierce battle in the morning, in which at least 12 opposition fighters and three Taleban militiamen had been killed.
They said seven Taleban fighters had been wounded in the two-pronged assault from the south and west.

The Soviet-built base, about 50 km (31 miles) north of Kabul, fell to the Taleban after they captured Kabul on September 27, but was retaken by former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood on October 18.
The Taleban grabbed it back on December 27, but could only hold it for a few hours.
The Taleban have been locked in see-saw battles with forces loyal to Masood and his ally, northern General Abdul Rashid Dostum, since the Islamic movement took Kabul.
The latest fighting came a day after U.N.-sponsored peace talks between the Taleban and its opponents ended inconclusively in Islamabad.
